# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 5

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 5 — The Way of Death
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 5

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: Opening framing — "full of curse" vs. "soaked in curse"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "evil and full of curse" |
| LOGOS | "evil and full of a curse" |
| PNEUMA | "thoroughly evil, soaked in curse" |

**Issue:** The Greek κατάρας μεστή = "full of curse." PNEUMA's "soaked in curse" is evocative but paraphrastic. The article ("a curse") in LOGOS is a minor addition.
**Ruling:** "Evil and full of curse" (EMET, without the article) adopted. The Greek has no article, and the weight of the anarthrous "curse" is appropriate.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: φθορεῖς πλάσματος θεοῦ — "image" vs. "what God formed"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "destroyers of the image of God" |
| LOGOS | "corruptors of what God has formed" |
| PNEUMA | "destroy what God has fashioned" |

**Issue:** πλάσμα = that which is molded/formed (Gen 2:7 allusion, not the εἰκών/image of Gen 1:27). EMET confuses the two creation theology terms.
**Ruling:** "Corruptors of what God has formed" (LOGOS) adopted. The allusion to Gen 2:7 is theologically significant and must be preserved.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.2: "meekness/gentleness" terminology

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "meekness and patience" |
| LOGOS | "gentleness and patience" |
| PNEUMA | "gentleness and patience" |

**Issue:** πραΰτης = meekness/gentleness (same word as Matt 5:5, Beatitudes). "Meekness" preserves the beatitude link; "gentleness" is more accessible.
**Ruling:** "Gentleness and patience" adopted (LOGOS/PNEUMA). The thematic echo of the Beatitudes is noted in the translator notes but "gentleness" is the clearer English term.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.2: "chasers of reward" vs. "pursuing reward"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "pursuing reward" |
| LOGOS | "chasers of reward" |
| PNEUMA | "live for profit" |

**Issue:** The Greek διώκοντες ἀνταπόδομα = pursuing/chasing recompense. The pejorative "chasers" captures the predatory quality better.
**Ruling:** "Chasers of reward" (LOGOS) adopted.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.2: Final closing — structural question

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "altogether sinful. Children, may you be delivered..." |
| LOGOS | "sinners in every way. Children, may you be delivered..." |
| PNEUMA | "In every possible way — sinners. Children, may you be kept from all of this." |

**Issue:** "Delivered" vs. "kept from." ῥυσθείητε = to be rescued/delivered (same root as the Lord's Prayer "deliver us from evil"). "Delivered" is more fitting and echoes the liturgical context.
**Ruling:** "May you be delivered from all of these" (EMET/LOGOS) adopted. The word "delivered" connects to ch. 8's Lord's Prayer and should be maintained.
